an8.52:1.1: At one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Vesālī, in the Great Wood, at the Gabled Hall.
an8.52:1.2: Then venerable Ānanda approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side. While sitting on one side venerable Ānanda said this to the Fortunate One:
an8.52:1.3: “With how many qualities, reverend Sir, should a monk who is authorised as an advisor to nuns be endowed?” “A monk endowed with eight qualities, Ānanda,
an8.52:2.1: should be authorised as an advisor to nuns,
an8.52:2.3: Here, Ānanda, a monk is virtuous, he trains in the training rules he has undertaken.
an8.52:2.5: Both Pātimokkhas are well passed down to him with the explanation, well-classified, well-recited, well-discerned in regard to the rule and the details.
an8.52:2.6: He is a beautiful speaker, a beautiful recitor, he is endowed with good speech, that is distinct, clear, that instructs in the meaning.
an8.52:2.7: He is able to talk in conformity with Dhamma to the Community of nuns, to instruct, rouse, enthuse, and cheer (them).
an8.52:2.8: He is dear and pleasing to almost all the nuns.
an8.52:2.9: ° In regard to one who has gone forth under the Fortunate One, who dwells wearing the ochre robe, he is not guilty of a serious offence.
an8.52:2.10: He has either twenty Rains Retreats or more than twenty Rains Retreats.
an8.52:2.11: A monk endowed with these eight qualities, Ānanda, should be authorised as an advisor to nuns.”
